**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant/part affected:** Cauliflower head (curd)
- **Key features observed:**
  - White cauliflower curd with distinct **dark brown to black necrotic lesions** concentrated on portions of the head
  - The darkened areas appear sunken, water-soaked, and mushy/rotted in texture
  - The rot is localized to specific sections of the curd, with soft, discolored tissue
  - The surrounding leaves appear relatively healthy with a normal blue-green color
  - No powdery/fuzzy growth (ruling out Downy Mildew), no leaf spots with halos (ruling out Alternaria), no V-shaped lesions on leaf margins (ruling out Black Rot)

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Alternaria Leaf Spot** — typically affects leaves with circular dark spots with yellow halos; not a curd rot pattern
- **Black Rot** — caused by *Xanthomonas campestris*, produces V-shaped yellow lesions on leaf margins, blackening of veins; primarily a leaf/vascular disease
- **Downy Mildew** — causes yellow patches on upper leaf surface with grayish-purple downy sporulation on undersides; not a curd rot
- **Bacterial Soft Rot** — caused by *Pectobacterium/Erwinia* spp.; produces water-soaked, soft, mushy, brown-to-black rotting lesions on the curd/head with a foul odor. The dark, sunken, wet-looking necrotic patches on the cauliflower curd are classic signs of bacterial soft rot.

The wet, mushy, dark brown-black decay on the cauliflower curd strongly matches **Bacterial Soft Rot**.
